gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the adapter you need for a full 25W depends on which charger you use: Apple's MagSafe Charger gets it with a 30 W adapter, ESR's Cyclone pad needs 35 W or more, and Anker's Prime foldable station needs 45 W or more. A 30 W adapter that is enough for Apple's charger is below what ESR and Anker say their 25W chargers need.
standout_why: I compared against apple.com/iphone-17/specs (cited) and the cited apple.com MagSafe Charger product pages. The specs page says only 'MagSafe wireless charging up to 25W with 30W power adapter or higher' and 'Qi2 wireless charging up to 25W'. It gives no adapter requirement for third-party Qi2.2 chargers. The MagSafe Charger page that loaded had only a testing footnote and no wattage table. ChatGPT's answer repeated '30W or higher adapter for Apple's MagSafe Charger' and said nothing about the higher adapter wattage that third-party Qi2.2 makers require. None of the rival pages notes that the iPhone Air in the same lineup tops out at 20W, or that Belkin's 'Series 16 and later charge at 25W' wording misses this.
decides: This settles the adapter column more than the pick. If the shopper already owns a 30 W USB-C adapter, Apple's MagSafe Charger is the only option here whose maker promises the full 25W with it. ESR's Cyclone needs 35 W and Anker's Prime foldable needs 45 W. Belkin's WIZ040 (45 W adapter in the box) and Anker's Prime dock A25X7 (65 W adapter in the box) remove the question. It also confirms that the base iPhone 17 gets the full 25W, while an iPhone Air owner tops out at 20W on any of these chargers.

findings.label: Wireless charging maximums and adapter condition
findings.value: MagSafe up to 25 W and Qi2 up to 25 W. The MagSafe 25 W needs a 30 W or larger adapter.
findings.note: Footnote 6: 'MagSafe wireless charging up to 25W with 30W power adapter or higher.' Apple tested with MagSafe Chargers A3502/A3503 and the Apple 30W (A2164) or 40W Dynamic (A3351) adapter. Apple claims 50% in 30 min over MagSafe with a 30 W+ adapter. The page gives no adapter condition for the Qi2 25 W.
